title: Warehouse's duty of care; contractual limitation of liability
summary: A warehouse is liable for loss or damage caused by its failure to take the care a reasonably careful person would take under similar circumstances. Liability may be limited per item or per unit weight in the warehouse receipt or storage agreement. This is model text: the law that binds is the version the state enacted (see that state's UCC Article 7 entry).
keyPoints: Limitations of liability must be stated in the receipt or storage agreement.
Check the 3PL agreement's liability cap against this baseline.
sourceAuthority: Cornell Legal Information Institute (unofficial copy of the ALI/ULC model text)

title: Lien of warehouse
summary: A warehouse has a lien on the goods it holds for storage and handling charges. This matters in billing disputes: a 3PL may hold inventory against unpaid invoices, so dispute specific lines in writing rather than withholding whole invoices.
sourceAuthority: Cornell Legal Information Institute (unofficial copy of the ALI/ULC model text)

title: Form of warehouse receipt; effect of omission
summary: Lists what a warehouse receipt should state (location, date, rate of storage and handling charges, description of goods, and so on). Useful for checking that the 3PL's receipts and rate disclosures are complete.
sourceAuthority: Cornell Legal Information Institute (unofficial copy of the ALI/ULC model text)

title: NMFC density-based classification
summary: LTL freight class is set by the NMFC, published by the National Motor Freight Traffic Association. The 2025 changes moved many items to a density-based scale. The auditor's density table (AuditSettings.DensityScale) should match the NMFC edition your carriers use.
keyPoints: The NMFC is a subscription publication; confirm the class for specific item numbers in ClassIT or the carrier tariff.
Commodities with a fixed item class are not rated by density.
notes: The homepage is a placeholder. Replace it with the docket or classification page your team uses.

title: GS1 Logistic Label (SSCC / GS1-128)
summary: The carton and pallet label standard most retailer routing guides build on (SSCC-18 in a GS1-128 barcode). Labeling chargebacks are usually tested against the retailer's routing guide, which references this standard.

title: ASC X12 856 Ship Notice/Manifest (ASN)
summary: The EDI transaction for advance ship notices. Retailer ASN chargebacks generally turn on timing and accuracy of the 856 against the physical shipment; keep 997 acknowledgments as proof of transmission time.
notes: Replace with the specific 856 page or the retailer's EDI implementation guide.

title: Best practice: 3PL billing controls
summary: Controls that make 3PL invoices auditable: a signed rate card with charge codes matching invoice codes; written approval for project, labor and special-handling charges; a monthly activity export from the WMS matched to invoice quantities; a defined storage billing method (anniversary vs. calendar, how partial months are handled); and a contractual dispute window with credit-memo terms.
keyPoints: Get the WMS activity export in the contract as a deliverable.
Agree in writing how a disputed line is handled so the 3PL can't place a lien on the whole balance.
notes: No external source. This entry is guidance and stays 'NeedsSource' until you link a source you trust (for example WERC or a CSCMP publication).
